title: loss:minecraft:banner/patterns
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Bedrock draws banner patterns from its own client assets and names them by a short code, so a pattern a datapack shipped has no code to be named by and the layer is dropped. Every pattern Java 26.3 publishes has one; no template uses a pattern that does not.

title: loss:minecraft:brewing_stand/Items[].components.minecraft:potion_contents
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Bedrock tells its potions apart by the stack's data value rather than by name, and no pinned source publishes which number is which potion, so a stack of a named potion arrives as the plain bottle. Three stacks in the templates are potions: two of strong healing in an end city, one splash potion of weakness in an igloo.

title: loss:minecraft:furnace/RecipesUsed
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Java tallies how many of each recipe a furnace smelted, to hand back the right experience. Bedrock keeps one number, `StoredXPInt`, and no recipe names. The 48 furnaces, blast furnaces and smokers in the templates carry the tally; one of them has anything in it.

title: loss:minecraft:sign/allow_op_features
context: Allow-listed difference
details: A Java sign may be allowed to run the click events an operator wrote into its text. Bedrock signs run nothing, so there is no flag to carry. All five signs in the structure templates set it.

title: loss:minecraft:sign/filtered_messages
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Java keeps a second, profanity-filtered copy of a sign's four lines for Realms. A Bedrock sign face holds one string, so only the unfiltered copy travels. One template sign carries the second copy.

title: loss:minecraft:trial_spawner/normal_config
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Java may write a trial spawner's two configurations as a reference into its `trial_spawner` registry, and all 14 in the templates do. Bedrock has no reference form and takes the configuration inline, so resolving one means reading the Java registry, which this server does not load. A configuration written inline translates.

title: untranslated:banner_pattern
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Bedrock names banner patterns by two-letter code rather than by identifier, and no pinned source publishes the pairing; Geyser keeps it in client code. It travels in the banner's block entity NBT, which lists patterns by a short code such as `bs` or `cr`.

title: untranslated:instrument
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Bedrock selects a goat horn sound by the item data value, in the order the eight horns were added; the identifiers exist only on the Java side. It travels in the goat horn item's data value, 0 to 7.

title: untranslated:painting_variant
context: Allow-listed difference
details: Bedrock paintings are named by the resource pack texture they draw, so the set a client knows is whatever its pack ships; the pinned metadata lists no painting registry. It travels in the painting entity's `Motive` string, which is a resource pack name rather than a registry id.
